newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Cellcom plans U.S. offering - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Cellcom plans U.S. offering - newspaper.

text.p: Cellcom, Israel's second cellular phone operator, refused to comment on a newspaper report that it is planning a public offering in the United States.
A spokeswoman for the Cellcom consortium said the company would not make any statement on the report in Sunday's Maariv newspaper.

According to the report, Cellcom plans to raise $150 million to $200 million in an initial public offering in the United States in the first quarter of 1997. The report said the company's valuation ranged from $750 million to $1 billion.
Cellcom is owned by Bellsouth Corp, Brazil's Safra banking family and Israel's Discount Investment Corp.
The company, which has 450,000 subscribers, began operations at the end of 1994 to compete with Israel's other cellular phone operator, a joint venture of Bezeq Israel Telecom and Motorola INc.
